correctness.rationale: The identity τ(τ(n))=(ω(A)+U+1)W follows by separating the power of two in τ(n). For fixed powerful β, the squarefree coprime counting density is (ζ(2)β)⁻¹∏p/(p+1), and the local mass sum at p, before the global ζ(2) factor, is 1+1/(p²−1). For the fixed-fiber Gaussian law the Dirichlet series is ζ(s)^z times an absolutely convergent analytic product near s=z=1 after finite exclusions. Uniform Selberg–Delange with z=exp(it/√log log y), divided by the z=1 count, gives the claimed centered characteristic function; the fixed shifts and replacement y=X/β do not contribute. The reciprocal sum over powerful β converges by β=u²v³ with v squarefree, giving tightness and justifying the finite-fiber limit and independence. Continuous mapping gives the mixture. The β=1 and β=4 masses make the variance mixing law nonconstant, hence not a single normal by uniqueness of the Laplace transform. The W=1 event requires e+1 to be a power of two at every prime; the discarded event at p>M has probability at most p⁻². As a separate bounded calculation, multiplying the stated factors over primes ≤10⁶, summing the powers e=0,1,3,7,15,31,63 (subsequent terms negligible), gives about 0.687827186, with Euler-product tail bounded by 10⁻⁶.
residual_risks: Uses classical uniform Selberg–Delange as an analytic input. The frozen finite tests are not a proof of the weak limit and are not independently attested. No rate or moment convergence is established.

value.rationale: The law explains why the unrestricted iterated divisor function does not have a single Gaussian fluctuation after fiber-dependent centering: repeated prime powers leave a discrete multiplicative scale even though the normalized prime-count fluctuations become independent. The explicit mixing law gives more information than the known first-order reciprocal average and distinguishes what can and cannot be inferred from an ordinary Erdős–Kac normalization.
residual_risks: The result is a qualitative distributional limit; it does not quantify approximation errors or moment behavior.
